vq6I6UO1xVEqwXZ2NS18.name: Laura Kurgan talk: your ideas
vq6I6UO1xVEqwXZ2NS18.why: The hard part isn't the reading, it's deciding what to say. One bridge sentence between her work and yours is enough. Each step below is a place you could stop with something useful in hand.

steps.t: Skim her essay, GPS for the Brain
steps.how: The opening and the section headings are enough. If something catches, jot one sentence on why she thinks a GPS dot is the wrong picture of how the brain maps space.

Two pages, mostly images. The detail worth knowing: in Barcelona she walked a museum roof with a GPS receiver and drew the word MUSEU. It's interesting to set that against naming a star on the horizon.
Three pairs, one line each: she locates by ___, the sky tradition locates by ___. Who holds the map? How is a place remembered? Rough is plenty. This is the heart of the hour.

steps.t: Pick two questions and one star
steps.how: Two questions from the list below, and one star name to bring, ideally one that can be shown on the actual sky that night.
The outline below can be pasted into the message, with the two questions and the star added. It can be rough, and it can be adjusted on the night.

lists.title: A shape for the conversation
items: Where are you? You Are Here: Museu versus naming a star at the horizon. Drawing with satellites versus drawing with names.
Who holds the map? GPS began as a military system, while sky knowledge belonged to a community. Add Million Dollar Blocks: who decides which data becomes visible?
How do we remember a place? The brain's "GPS" versus poems and star names as memory tools.
Back to this sky. The triennial is about civic infrastructure. Is the sky one? Who looks after it, and who is allowed to read it?

lists.title: Questions you could ask her
items: When you first used GPS as a drawing tool, what did the satellite not know about the building?
If GPS is the wrong metaphor for a cognitive map, what would you choose?
What do you think is lost when a place becomes a coordinate?
Is a poem a data format?

lists.title: Questions she may ask you
items: Why does a star name hold more than its position?
What did computation fail to hold when you translated the poems?

vq6I6UO1xVEqwXZ2NS18.note: Check her essay before you quote it. I'm not certain about the details of her GPS for the Brain talk.
